filename: Evolution of Tropical Cyclone Properties Across the Development Cycle of the GISS-E3 Global Climate Model.pdf
title: Evolution of Tropical Cyclone Properties Across the Development Cycle of the GISS-E3 Global Climate Model
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
code_availability: Jupyter (Russotto et al., 2021) notebooks used to do the analysis and data files necessary to reproduce figures are posted online at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5542663
testbed_rationale: The study conducts climate model evaluation and parameter perturbation experiments using traditional physics parameterizations without machine learning components or standardized benchmark formatting for ML training.
pain_points: Underestimation of tropical cyclone frequency and maximum intensity compared to real-world observations
Compensating errors where increasing entrainment improves TC counts but exacerbates global radiative imbalances and cloud/precipitation biases
Large computational expense of high-resolution (0.5 degree) multidecadal GCM simulations
Missing 3D high-frequency simulation fields for version 2 (V2) preventing detailed storm structure diagnostics
extraction_notes: The paper does not apply machine learning. It investigates physical parameter sensitivity (entrainment rates and divergence damping) and physical parameterization changes across two development versions of GISS-E3 at 0.5-degree resolution.
